intro: You've been searching for a crypto accountant near you, which usually means you have activity on exchanges or wallets and want it reported properly to HMRC. Local knowledge helps here, because crypto gains and income follow specific UK rules and a nearby accountant can talk you through them. Tell us what you hold and what you've done with it, and we'll introduce you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a crypto accountant usually need
need_lead: Most people who look for a crypto accountant near them are trying to make sense of transactions that don't fit neatly into a standard tax return.
needs: You have bought, sold or swapped cryptoassets and need the gains worked out using HMRC's pooling rules rather than a simple difference between buying and selling prices.
You have received staking rewards or airdrops and are unsure whether these count as income, and if so how they should be reported.
You have traded across several exchanges and wallets and need help pulling a complete transaction history together before anything is calculated.
You are worried about records that are incomplete or spread over old platforms and want someone to help you reconstruct what happened.
You want to report your crypto activity correctly on your tax return and would rather have an accountant check the figures before you file.
context_heading: What to understand about crypto and HMRC
context: HMRC treats cryptoassets as property for tax purposes, and disposals such as selling, swapping one coin for another or spending crypto can give rise to capital gains. The calculations use pooling rules, which is why a full transaction history from every exchange and wallet matters so much. Staking rewards and airdrops can create income tax as well, so they need to be looked at separately from gains.

HMRC can obtain information from exchanges, so gaps in your records are worth addressing rather than leaving. In the UK the word "accountant" on its own is not a protected title, but titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected and their members are bound by their body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Every practice offering accountancy services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: List the exchanges and wallets you have used, including any you no longer have access to.
Say roughly what kinds of activity you have had, such as buying and selling, swapping, staking, airdrops or spending crypto.
Mention whether you have kept transaction records or exported histories, and whether anything is missing.
Explain which tax years are involved and whether you have already filed a return covering any crypto activity.
Say whether you are an individual, or whether the activity sits inside a business or company.
Note anything that makes your situation unusual, such as lost exchange access, a move to or from the UK, or gifts of crypto.
questions: Which body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and how are complaints handled?
How will you work out my gains, and will you use HMRC's pooling rules?
How should staking rewards and airdrops be treated in my case?
What records or exports do you need from each exchange and wallet?
Will you explain the figures to me before anything is filed?

faqs.q: Do I need to declare crypto on my UK tax return?
faqs.a: If you have disposed of cryptoassets, for example by selling, swapping or spending them, any gain may need to be reported depending on your circumstances. Staking rewards and airdrops can also count as income. An accountant can look at your transactions and tell you what applies to you.

faqs.q: What if I've lost access to an old exchange?
faqs.a: It happens, and it's worth mentioning when you enquire. Your transaction history may still be recoverable through records you hold or the exchange itself, and an accountant can advise on how to handle gaps. HMRC can obtain information from exchanges, so it's better to address missing records openly.

faqs.q: How do I choose a crypto accountant near me?
faqs.a: Ask which professional body supervises the practice, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and how complaints are handled. Check whether they are comfortable with the specific activity you have, such as staking or swaps, and ask them to explain their approach before you commit. Quotes are on application, so compare what each professional offers.

faqs.q: Can I just use the figures from my exchange?
faqs.a: Exchange summaries can be a helpful starting point, but they may not apply HMRC's pooling rules or separate income from gains. Exporting complete histories from every exchange and wallet gives a clearer picture. An accountant can then work through the figures properly.
